rv.q: The verdict, therefore, remains out as to both the depth of his performance and the pacing of the show in general.
There’s very little here to justify yet another look at Bruce’s downfall, much less to demonstrate what a great standup we lost thereby.
However, Susan Charlotte’s adaptation does not do the material justice.
Unfortunately, The People Versus Lenny Bruce lets our minds wander, so we notice.

Anthony’s performance captures Lenny’s urgency while taking moments to recognize the absurdity of being dragged into court over words, and struggling with being denied a chance to perform his act in court.
Except for Bruce’s meandering monologue at the end of the play, the piece moves along.

cn.t: Critics find this courtroom drama about Lenny Bruce's obscenity trial timely but muddled in execution, with bland direction undermining the compelling subject matter. Reception ranges from respectful to disappointed.
